headline: Quantum theory, circuit efficiency, and thermal dynamics
summary: Today's papers bridge foundational quantum questions and computational scalability. Work spans a no-go theorem on measurement realism, universal deep thermalization under noise, and major algorithmic speedups in both classical tensor-network and randomized quantum Hamiltonian simulation.

themes.title: Quantum Simulation & Algorithm Optimization
themes.body: StateDRIFT and ArcTN tackle resource bottlenecks from complementary sides—slashing quantum gate counts via adaptive term sampling and accelerating classical tensor-network circuit simulation FLOPs.

themes.title: Thermalization & Open Quantum Dynamics
themes.body: New analytical insights prove size-independent rapid mixing for quantum Gibbs samplers and show how noisy scrambling universally collapses mixed states toward Choi-state ensembles.

themes.title: Quantum Foundations
themes.body: A rigorous no-go theorem demonstrates that standard quantum measurement cannot be understood as discovering preexisting true values under probe-system entanglement.

connections.body: Both StateDRIFT and the solid oxide cell study focus on reducing quantum resource overheads for correlated molecular and materials problems to make practical simulation viable.
Both 2610.31580 and 2610.31571 examine the asymptotic behavior of dissipative and noisy quantum processes, linking error channels and thermal relaxation to steady-state structure.
